options: Bright red on paper or stool surface
Severe sharp anal pain during/after passage
Crampy abdominal pain relieved by defecation

history.ask: Weight loss or loss of appetite
Bloating with stress-related pattern, relief after defecation
Polyuria, kidney stones, or bone pain
Fluid intake, dietary fiber, physical activity
Vomiting or inability to pass gas

red_flags: Absolute constipation (no stool, no flatus) with vomiting and distension
Family history of colorectal cancer with any new bowel symptom
exam: Palpate the abdomen for masses and fecal loading along the colon
Look for distension and auscultate bowel sounds
Inspect the anus before inserting a finger — fissure, hemorrhoids, skin tags
Digital rectal examination: mass, stool impaction, sphincter tone, blood on glove
Check conjunctivae and palms for pallor
Look for hypothyroid signs: bradycardia, dry coarse skin, delayed ankle-reflex relaxation
Test distal sensation and ankle reflexes in diabetics — peripheral neuropathy accompanies enteric neuropathy
Record weight and compare with previous visits
Examine hernial orifices if obstruction is suspected

investigations.why: Iron-deficiency anemia with new constipation points to colorectal carcinoma until excluded
Raised TSH rules hypothyroidism in as the cause of new constipation with cold intolerance or weight gain
Rules hypercalcemia (and hypokalemia) in or out — reversible metabolic causes behind polyuria, stones, or bone pain
Confirms poorly controlled diabetes when autonomic enteric neuropathy is suspected
Baseline renal function — chronic hypercalcemia and dehydration from poor intake both injure the kidney and change the picture
Shows fecal impaction or air–fluid levels when obstruction or severe loading with vomiting is the question
Second-line — if any alarm feature (age > 50 new onset, bleeding, weight loss, narrowing caliber, iron-deficiency anemia): rules colorectal carcinoma in or out

supports: Lifelong pattern of hard, infrequent stool
Normal examination apart from fecal loading
Bloating and crampy pain relieved by defecation
No blood, no weight loss, normal exam
Dark blood mixed with stool or narrowing caliber
Weight loss, rectal mass, or pallor
Onset after starting opioids, iron, calcium-channel blockers, or anticholinergics
Bradycardia, dry skin, delayed ankle reflexes
Distal sensory loss and absent ankle reflexes
No stool or flatus with vomiting
Hernia or abdominal mass on exam
